title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC invented quamprimum; GAR effect/poena
pass_a_gloss: If 'quamprimum' was not in the covenant wording, why did the learned man add it? If God did use it, why take it so tightly as to shut out the habit just because actual sin may have been followed by a nature-moment rather than a time-moment? GAR then compares actual disobedience with ensuing habitual corruption: the latter is effect and just penalty of the former; penalty is not imputed—only the meritorious sin—so of course the disobedience is charged rather than the corruption.
pass_b_english: But if the word 'as soon as' (quamprimum) was absent from those words in which it was conceived, why did the learned man insert and add it of his own? If in conceiving that covenant God used that word, whence does the learned man have it that it is to be taken in so precise a sense as to exclude the habit for this reason—that if not by some moment of time, perhaps by a moment of nature, actual sin was followed? GAR. If a comparison is instituted between Adam's actual disobedience and the ensuing habitual corruption, we shall see that this corruption was an effect of that disobedience, and so a penalty by God's just judgment of that actual sin. But penalty is not imputed; rather the sin which is the meritorious cause of that penalty. What wonder, then, if that disobedience was rather imputed than this corruption?
source_text: Quod si vox quamprimum abfuit ab illis verbis quibus conceptum fuit, cur eam vir doctus de suo inseruit & addidit? Si in concipiendo illo foedere Deus illa voce usus est, unde habet vir doctus eam significatione tam praecisa esse accipiendam, ut excludat habitum ideo, quia si non temporis forte aliquo naturae momento secutus est actuale peccatum? GAR. Si comparatio instituatur actualis inobedientiae Adami, & consecuta corruptionis habitualis, videbimus hanc corruptionem fuisse effectum illius inobedientiae, atque adeo poenam justo Dei judicio illius peccati actualis. Poena vero non imputatur, sed peccatum potius quod est illius poenae causa meritoria. Quid ergo mirum, si illa inobedientia potius imputata est, quam ista corruptio?

choices.choice: Placeus on inserted quamprimum; GAR: corruption as penalty-effect
